title: Format a price for Germany, then parseFloat it back, and 1234.56 becomes 1.234
assumption: A number you formatted for display with Intl.NumberFormat can be read back with parseFloat to recover the same value.

input.description: A price formatted for a German user as "1.234,56" (period as thousands separator, comma as decimal separator) that later gets fed back into the same parsing code path used for US-formatted input, e.g. a form field pre-filled with a locale-formatted value and then re-parsed on submit.

what_goes_wrong: `new Intl.NumberFormat("de-DE").format(1234.56)` correctly produces the German-formatted string "1.234,56" - but `parseFloat("1.234,56")` reads that back as `1.234`, not `1234.56`: it treats the German thousands-separating period as a decimal point and stops at the comma.
why: `Intl.NumberFormat` is locale-aware in one direction only: it formats a number according to the target locale's conventions (in de-DE, "." groups thousands and "," is the decimal mark). `parseFloat`, by contrast, is not locale-aware at all - it only ever understands JavaScript's own numeric literal syntax, where "." is always the decimal point. Feeding a de-DE-formatted string into a locale-blind parser silently reinterprets the grouping separator as the decimal point, truncating the value by roughly three orders of magnitude.

repros.code:
# Python's stdlib has no locale-formatting function comparable to Intl.NumberFormat
# without opting into the system locale database; the bug is demonstrated directly
# by parsing a German-formatted string the same naive way.
formatted = "1.234,56"
try:
    print(float(formatted))
except ValueError as e:
    print("ValueError:", e)
repros.expected_output: ValueError: could not convert string to float: '1.234,56'

fix: Never round-trip a locale-formatted display string through a locale-blind parser. Keep the underlying numeric value (not its formatted string) as the source of truth, and if you must parse locale-formatted input, use `Intl.NumberFormat(locale).formatToParts()` to discover that locale's actual group/decimal characters first.

test_cases.note: A their_parse_price(str, locale) function given the de-DE-formatted "1.234,56" should return 1234.56, not the 1.234 that locale-blind parseFloat gives.
